raw.title: Regional AP Technology Manager - East
raw.excerpt: Be Part of an Amazing StoryMacy’s is more than just a store.
raw.description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

The Manager, Regional Asset Protection Technology supports stores, field teams, and Asset Protection leaders within an assigned region by managing, maintaining, and improving Asset Protection technology solutions and operational processes. Guided by service and anticipation, this role serves as the primary regional liaison for AP technology initiatives, supporting the deployment, troubleshooting, maintenance, and optimization of technology solutions that strengthen Asset Protection effectiveness and operational performance.

The Manager, Regional AP Technology partners closely with the Senior Manager, AP Technology, Division Asset Protection Directors, store leadership, Macy's Technology, vendors, and cross-functional business partners to ensure AP technology solutions remain reliable, effective, and aligned with operational needs. This role coordinates work orders, technology repairs, maintenance activities, local project execution, budgeting support, and vendor engagement across the region. Success requires strong relationship-building, project coordination, operational problem-solving, and technology support capabilities.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as the primary regional contact for Asset Protection technology solutions supporting stores and field teams within an assigned territory.

  • Support the implementation, adoption, and ongoing operation of Asset Protection technologies, including video management systems, RFID solutions, investigative technologies, exception reporting tools, and related platforms.

  • Manage and monitor technology-related work orders, service requests, and repair activities to ensure timely resolution and minimal operational disruption.

  • Coordinate technology maintenance and repair activities with vendors, Macy's Technology teams, store leadership, and Asset Protection partners.

  • Troubleshoot technology issues and partner with Technology teams and vendors to identify root causes and implement effective solutions.

  • Conduct store visits and field assessments to evaluate technology performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and ensure operational standards are maintained.

  • Partner with Division Asset Protection Directors and field leaders to prioritize technology needs and support regional operational objectives.

  • Support regional technology budgeting processes by tracking expenses, monitoring project costs, and assisting with budget planning activities.

  • Coordinate local technology projects, installations, upgrades, pilot programs, and equipment replacement initiatives across the region.

  • Assist with proof-of-concept testing and pilot evaluations by gathering feedback, documenting results, and supporting implementation planning.

  • Monitor technology performance and operational issues to identify recurring trends, risks, and enhancement opportunities.

  • Provide guidance and support to store and field teams regarding technology functionality, troubleshooting, and operational best practices.

  • Partner with vendors to coordinate service delivery, installations, repairs, inspections, and ongoing maintenance activities.

  • Support technology-related training efforts and reinforce adoption of new tools, processes, and capabilities.

  • Maintain accurate records related to technology assets, work orders, repairs, project status, and budget expenditures.

  • Support risk assessments, operational reviews, and compliance initiatives associated with AP technology solutions.

  • Communicate project updates, repair status, operational challenges, and technology recommendations to regional and corporate leadership.

  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships and ensures authentic connections with colleagues, customers, and communities.

  • In addition to the essential duties mentioned above, other duties may be assigned.

Skills You Will Need

Asset Protection Technology: Knowledge of Asset Protection technologies, including video management systems, RFID solutions, investigative platforms, exception reporting tools, and related operational technologies.

Technology Troubleshooting: Ability to diagnose operational and technology issues, identify root causes, and coordinate effective resolutions with technical teams and vendors.

Vendor Management: Experience working with external vendors, service providers, installers, and maintenance partners to ensure quality service and accountability.

Project Coordination: Ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously while coordinating resources, timelines, stakeholders, and project deliverables.

Operational Support: Strong understanding of store operations and Asset Protection processes with the ability to align technology solutions to business needs.

Budget Administration: Ability to monitor spending, track expenses, support forecasting activities, and assist with regional budget management.

Relationship Building: Ability to develop productive partnerships with store leaders, field teams, vendors, Technology partners, and Asset Protection leadership.

Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across multiple organizational levels.

Organization and Prioritization: Ability to manage competing priorities, track multiple work streams, and maintain strong attention to detail.

Change Management: Ability to support implementation efforts, user adoption, training initiatives, and operational transitions.

Problem-Solving: Demonstrated ability to assess situations, develop practical solutions, and drive successful outcomes.

Adaptability and Initiative: Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment and effectively responds to changing priorities and business needs.

Integrity and Professionalism: Commitment to exemplifying the highest standards of ethics, confidentiality, and professional conduct.

Who You Are

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Criminal Justice, Asset Protection, Information Systems, Technology Management, Operations, or a related field preferred; equivalent work experience will also be considered.

  • 3+ years of experience in Asset Protection, retail operations, technology support, systems administration, project coordination, or a related discipline.

  • Experience supporting technology deployments, operational projects, maintenance programs, or field support activities preferred.

  • Knowledge of retail technology, video systems, RFID technology, security systems, investigative technologies, or related operational platforms preferred.

  • Experience managing vendors, service providers, maintenance requests, or operational support functions.

  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while supporting stores and field organizations across a large geographic region.

  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across multiple levels of the organization.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams.

  • Regularly required to sit, talk, hear, and use hands/fingers to operate computer systems and technology. Frequently required to travel, move about store and operational environments, and inspect technology installations. Requires close vision.

  • Able to work a flexible schedule based on department and company needs, including overnight travel and occasional weekend support as required.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts

  • Performance-based incentives

  • Annual merit review

  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

  • Tuition reimbursement

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - apply today!

This job description is not all-inclusive. Macy's, Inc. reserves the right to amend this job description at any time. Macy's, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment.

raw.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe is a global technology company that builds infrastructure for online commerce with a mission to increase the GDP of the internet. Through Bridge, Stripe is building stablecoin infrastructure that helps businesses move, store, and use money globally. This role will support Bridge as it develops and scales products for companies operating across markets.

What you’ll do

Stripe is looking for an exceptional transactional lawyer to join our commercial legal team supporting Bridge and Stripe’s fast-growing stablecoin business.

Responsibilities

  • Support Bridge’s commercial team, leading negotiations for complex and strategic user and partner agreements.
  • Advise on commercial and legal issues arising from stablecoin products, new product launches, and international expansion.
  • Work closely with Product Legal and Bridge’s product and engineering teams to bring new products and features to market.
  • Help build Bridge’s commercial legal infrastructure so the business can scale efficiently, including drafting and maintaining agreements and playbooks, improving internal processes, and using AI tooling to optimize how we work with clients, partners, and users.
  • Partner with teams across Bridge and Stripe globally, including commercial, operations, product, engineering, tax, compliance, and risk.
  • Help the team provide practical, scalable legal support while working collaboratively across a global Commercial Legal team.
  • Develop and deliver training and resources to help Bridge’s commercial team sell and support its products.
  • Be a point of escalation for outside counsel.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • Intellectually curious and a creative problem solver - Bridge’s products and the stablecoin industry are complex and fast evolving - you should relish learning new products and finding practical solutions to challenging problems.
  • A self-starter with a bias for action - you are proactive and have a strong sense of ownership.
  • A clear and concise communicator (in written and verbal forms), who can distill the key risks and explain complex, nuanced issues in plain and simple terms.
  • A natural collaborator, able to guide cross-functional teams and drive to a win-win solution.
  • Familiar with the legal issues and commercial risks arising from fintech, stablecoin, hosted data, and technology services.
  • A team player who is willing to do what it takes to contribute to the collective success.
  • Qualified with good standing membership in at least one US state bar with a JD degree or foreign equivalent.
  • 8+ years of relevant experience in-house or in a technology practice group in a top law firm.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience working in payments, fintech, crypto, or stablecoin businesses and knowledge of associated regulatory issues.
  • In-house experience advising high-growth companies.
  • Working knowledge of LLM tools.
  • Experience in improving legal processes with AI technology.
  • A working knowledge of data protection laws such as CCPA, GDPR, and HIPAA.

raw.description:
Bright Vision Technologies is a forward-thinking software development company dedicated to building innovative solutions that help businesses automate and optimize their operations. We leverage cutting-edge technologies to create scalable, secure, and user-friendly applications.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a skilled ServiceNow Application Developer to join our dynamic team and contribute to our mission of transforming business processes through technology.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: ServiceNow Application Developer

Salary: $120K - $170 K

Employment Terms & Visa Policy
This is a 100% remote, full-time, direct W2 position with Bright Vision Technologies.
This role is part of Bright Vision Technologies’ in-house Statement of Work (SOW) engagement. The client, end customer, and employer for this position is Bright Vision Technologies — there is no third-party client, vendor, or implementation partner involved.

We do not engage in C2C, 1099, or third-party arrangements for this role.
Candidates must be willing to work directly as a full-time W2 employee of Bright Vision Technologies and contribute to our in-house SOW deliverables.

No new H1B sponsorship is available for this role.
However, candidates who are currently on a valid H1B visa and require a transfer are welcome to apply. We will support H1B transfers for qualified candidates.

For every role, a technical coding assessment is mandatory. Please apply only if you are confident in your technical abilities and hands-on experience.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced ServiceNow Application Developer to build and maintain solutions across ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, CSM, and custom scoped applications. The role focuses on hands-on configuration and development — including workflows, Flow Designer, scripting, integrations, UI customization, and platform extensions — while applying best practices that keep the platform clean, upgrade-safe, and performant. The ideal candidate has shipped meaningful ServiceNow work in production, balances declarative and programmatic approaches thoughtfully, and writes maintainable code that survives upgrades and team turnover.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design and develop ServiceNow solutions across ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, CSM, and custom scoped applications.
  • Build workflows using Flow Designer, IntegrationHub, and Process Automation Designer where appropriate.
  • Write clean, well-tested server-side and client-side scripts (Business Rules, Script Includes, Client Scripts, UI Actions).
  • Develop scoped applications that follow platform best practices and avoid global-scope pollution.
  • Build integrations with enterprise systems using IntegrationHub spokes, REST/SOAP APIs, and MID Servers.
  • Develop catalog items, request workflows, and end-to-end fulfillment automation that simplify how users request services and ensure each request is routed, approved, and executed reliably end-to-end.
  • Implement Service Portal, Employee Center, and custom portal experiences using widgets and AngularJS.
  • Develop and maintain CMDB integrations, identification rules, and data quality improvements.
  • Implement reports, dashboards, and Performance Analytics where required, ensuring stakeholders have the operational visibility they need to monitor service performance and make informed decisions.
  • Participate in design reviews, contribute to platform standards, and document technical decisions.
  • Support upgrades, regression testing, and remediation of customizations across releases.
  • Troubleshoot performance, scripting, and integration issues across development, test, and production instances, applying systematic root-cause analysis and contributing durable fixes back to the platform.
  • Collaborate with admins, BAs, and stakeholders to refine requirements and propose pragmatic technical solutions.
  • Stay current with ServiceNow releases, new features, and emerging best practices.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Five or more years of hands-on ServiceNow development experience.
  • Strong JavaScript skills including ES5/ES6 patterns used in ServiceNow.
  • Deep expertise with Business Rules, Script Includes, Client Scripts, UI Actions, and UI Policies.
  • Experience with Flow Designer and IntegrationHub.
  • Hands-on integration experience using REST, SOAP, and MID Servers.
  • Strong understanding of the ServiceNow data model and CMDB concepts.
  • Experience with Service Portal widget development.
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) credential.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
Preferred Qualifications
  • ServiceNow Certified Application Developer (CAD).
  • Certified Implementation Specialist credentials (ITSM, HR, CSM, ITOM).
  • Experience with Now Assist or GenAI Controller.
  • Familiarity with App Engine Studio.
  • Exposure to multi-instance ServiceNow environments.

How to Apply

For immediate consideration, please send your resume to or contact us at (908) 505-3544. Learn more about Bright Vision Technologies at www.bvteck.com.

raw.excerpt: About Care AccessCare Access is working to make the future of health better for all.
raw.description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

The Leave of Absence Manager is responsible for administering the Company’s leave of absence programs and ensuring compliant, compassionate, and consistent support for employees and managers. This role serves as the subject matter expert for leave administration, ADA accommodations, and workers’ compensation, while also supporting employee continuity during emergencies and serving as the HR point of contact for safety-related matters.

This role also serves as a cross-trained backup and active contributor to the Benefits team, supporting day-to-day administration of health, welfare, and retirement plans. The ideal candidate combines deep leave-compliance expertise with the versatility to step into benefits administration as workload and coverage require.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Leave of Absence Administration
    • Own the end-to-end administration of employee leaves of absence, including FMLA, state and local leave programs, paid family and medical leave, parental leave, military leave, personal leave, and other Company-sponsored leave programs.
    • Partner with brokers and vendors to evaluate plan performance, ensure service excellence, and optimize cost-effectiveness. 
    • Serve as the primary point of contact for employees and managers throughout the leave process, providing clear, empathetic, and timely guidance on eligibility, required documentation, benefits continuation, pay coordination, and return-to-work expectations.
    • Ensure timely and accurate completion of leave notices, certifications, designation communications, payroll coordination, and related documentation.
    • Maintain accurate leave records in HRIS and leave-management systems; monitor leave balances, intermittent leave usage, and return-to-work dates.
    • Partner with Payroll, Benefits, HR Business Partners, managers, and external leave vendors to ensure leave information is administered consistently and accurately.
    • Stay current on applicable federal, state, and local leave laws and recommend process or policy updates as requirements change.
    • Develop reporting and identify trends, risks, and opportunities to improve the employee leave experience and operational effectiveness.
  • ADA Accommodation Processing
    • Manage the interactive process for workplace accommodation requests under the ADA and applicable state and local laws.
    • Review medical documentation, assess accommodation options, engage employees and managers in the interactive process, and document decisions and next steps.
    • Partner with HR Business Partners, Legal, and business leaders to implement reasonable accommodations and monitor ongoing effectiveness.
    • Maintain confidential accommodation records and ensure consistent, compliant handling of requests.
    • Workers Compensation
    • Coordinate the administration of workers’ compensation claims, including employee communications, claim reporting, documentation, and coordination with insurance carriers, third-party administrators, medical providers, and internal stakeholders.
    • Partner with managers and Safety team members to support timely incident reporting, return-to-work planning, and transitional-duty arrangements where appropriate.
    • Monitor open claims, identify trends, and escalate potential risks or process concerns.
  • Emergency Response and Employee Continuity
    • Support emergency-response activities related to natural disasters or other events that may affect employees’ ability to work.
    • Coordinate with HR leadership, business continuity teams, Payroll, Benefits, and managers to identify affected employees and provide timely guidance on available leave, pay, benefits, and support resources.
    • Help maintain employee-facing communications and procedures for HR-related emergency response.
  • Vaccination Records and Safety Team Support
    • Oversee the secure collection, tracking, and maintenance of employee vaccination records, as required by Company policy.
    • Serve as the initial HR point of contact for safety tickets requiring HR involvement, ensuring concerns are triaged, documented, and routed to the appropriate stakeholders.
    • Partner with the Safety team to support employee communications, incident follow-up, and compliance-related initiatives.
    • Maintain confidentiality and appropriate recordkeeping for safety and health-related information.
  • Other Responsbilities:
    • Serves as a cross-trained backup and active contributor to the Benefits Manager as needed
    • Support and contribute towards special projects as needed

The Expertise Required

  • Strong knowledge of ERISA, ACA, HIPAA, COBRA, FMLA, ADA, and other applicable laws. 
  • Experience working with medical leave and disability vendors; familiarity with leave case management best practices   
  • Demonstrated experience managing workers’ compensation processes and coordinating return-to-work programs.
  • Strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local employment laws related to leave, accommodations, workers’ compensation, and benefits continuation.
  • Experience working with HRIS, leave-management platforms, and case-management or ticketing systems; UKG experience is preferred.
  • Ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism.
  • Exceptional organization, follow-through, communication, and customer-service skills.
  • Ability to independently manage a high volume of cases, balance competing priorities, and communicate complex requirements in clear, compassionate language.

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education:
    • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered.
  • Minimum Experience:
    • 5+ years of progressive experience administering employee leaves of absence, including FMLA, ADA accommodations, and state and local leave programs.
    • Experience participating in or supporting HR, leave-management, benefits, or related vendor implementations is preferred.

How We Work Together

  • Location: Remote within the United States. This role requires 100% of work to be performed in a remote office environment.
  • Travel: This is a remote position with less than 10% travel requirements. Occasional planned travel may be required as part of the role.
  • Physical demands associated with this position Include: The ability to use keyboards and other computer equipment.

The expected pay range for this role is $70,000 - $100,000 USD per year for full time team members.

Benefits & Perks (US Full Time Employees)

  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and Company Paid Holidays
  • 100% Employer paid medical, dental, and vision insurance plan options
  • Health Savings Account and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Bi-weekly HSA employer contribution
  • Company paid Short-Term Disability and Long-Term Disability
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan, with Company Match

raw.excerpt: Spyre Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients.
raw.description:
Spyre Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients. Spyre's pipeline includes investigational extended half-life antibodies targeting α4β7, TL1A, IL-23, and IL-17A/F as well as rational combination programs.

Role Summary:

  • As the Director, Regulatory Affairs, you will play a key role in managing and overseeing regulatory affairs activities and execution within our organization, initially focused on Spyre’s IBD program. You will be responsible for planning and executing regulatory strategies that enable Spyre to initiate and manage clinical trials. You will also contribute to preclinical, CMC, and clinical development plans with the goal of ensuring Spyre performs the necessary studies to gain and maintain product approval(s) that are consistent with our target product profile(s).
  • You will act as the overall lead of global regulatory applications for one or more drug candidates and will lead the submission of original investigational new drug and clinical trial applications. You will lead efforts to plan and prepare for meetings with global health authorities (Type C & EOP2 meetings with FDA, EMA scientific advice, etc.) and support live discussions. You will also support the team by contributing to the development of other assets for which you are not the overall lead, and by contributing to the development of processes for the Regulatory Department.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Regulatory Strategy: Develop and implement regulatory strategies that enable the company’s clinical trials and marketing applications. Stay current with evolving regulatory requirements and industry trends and advise the company on regulatory expectations.
  • Regulatory Submissions: Prepare, review, and submit regulatory applications and dossiers to health authorities, such as the FDA, EMA, PMDA, and other global regulatory agencies, ensuring timely and successful approvals.
  • Health Authority Meetings: Plan meeting strategy, lead the development of briefing materials, capture action items, and support the team in implementation and strategy.
  • Communication: Represent the company in regulatory interactions and maintain effective communication with regulatory agencies, responding to inquiries and requests in a professional and efficient manner. Communicate regulatory agency interactions and guidance to Regulatory Affairs leadership and cross-functional teams.
  • Risk Management: Identify potential regulatory risks and proactively develop strategies to mitigate them. Monitor changes in regulatory landscapes and assess their impact on the company's products.
  • Regulatory Intelligence: Keep abreast of new and evolving regulations, guidelines, and best practices in the pharmaceutical industry and adapt company strategies accordingly.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate with other departments, including Pre-clinical Research & Development, Clinical Development, Technical Operations, Legal, and Quality and Compliance to ensure regulatory considerations are integrated into the product development process.
  • Budget Management: Contribute to development and management of the regulatory affairs budget for assigned projects, ensuring cost-effective use of resources while maintaining high-quality regulatory activities.

Ideal Candidate:

  • Bachelor’s degree with 8-10 years of experience in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs and/or related disciplines, or an equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience.
  • Proven track record of successfully managing complex regulatory submissions
  • Proven experience managing clinical trial applications in the US and globally
  • Strong knowledge of global pharmaceutical regulations and guidelines, including FDA, EMA, and ICH requirements
  • Proficient in medical and/or technical writing, including the ability to author or contribute to documents such as Module 2 and 3 summaries, DSURs, safety reports, investigational brochures, clinical trial protocols, clinical trial reports, and/or IMPDs
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • Strong problem-solving and critical thinking abilities
  • Ability to meet deadlines and adapt to changing priorities
  • Proficiency in regulatory affairs software and document management systems.
  • Experience with CMC regulatory, device (e.g., pre-filled syringe and/or auto-injector) and/or diagnostic (e.g., companion diagnostics)

What We Offer:

  • Opportunity to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where you help shape the culture of our young company, contribute broadly to advance meaningful medicines, and learn quickly.
  • Market competitive compensation and benefits package, including base salary, performance bonus, equity grant opportunities, health, welfare & retirement benefits.
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Two, one-week company-wide shutdowns each
  • Commitment to provide professional development opportunities.
  • Remote working environment with frequent in-person meetings to address complex problems and build relationships.

The expected salary range offer for this role is $220,000 to $245,000. Actual pay offered may vary depending on job related knowledge, experience, education, and geographic location.

As an equal opportunity employer, Spyre is committed to a diverse workforce. Employment decisions regarding recruitment and selection will be made without discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, genetic information or characteristic, gender identity and expression, veteran status, or other non-job-related characteristics or other prohibited grounds specified in applicable federal, state and local laws. We also embrace differences in experience and background, and welcome diversity of opinions and thought with active recruitment designed to create a stronger and better Spyre that is focused on developing life-changing products for patients.

raw.title: Sr. Revenue Enablement Manager, Partnerships & Supply
raw.excerpt: About EngineEngine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel.
raw.description:
About Engine

Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents.

That work has earned Engine recognition as TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), a spot on Inc.'s Power Partners list (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Your Mission:

As Revenue Enablement Manager, Partnership & Supply, you'll be the dedicated enablement partner for the teams that build and grow Engine's relationships with hotel and lodging partners. Our supply is a core part of what makes Engine work, and these teams keep it strong. New-hire onboarding is owned by a partner team. You own everything after it: ongoing enablement and everboarding that help partner and supply teams sign, activate, and grow partners. You'll report to the Manager, Revenue Enablement once that role is filled, and to the Director of Revenue Enablement until then. Here's what you'll take charge of:

Own Partnership & Supply Enablement

  • Everboarding Programs: Plan, build, and deliver training after onboarding for partner and supply teams, including skill-building paths, refreshers, and certifications on Engine's partner value proposition, programs, and processes.
  • Partner Sales Motion: Build and maintain the certification programs, training, job aids, and playbooks behind our partner sales motion, covering areas such as partner acquisition, negotiation, activation, and growing existing partner relationships.
  • Content & Knowledge Management: Keep partner and supply documentation, playbooks, and knowledge resources current and easy to find.
  • Onboarding Alignment: Partner with the onboarding team so what's learned in onboarding carries through once reps are ramped.
  • AI-First Enablement: Build AI first. Use AI to create partner certifications, job aids, playbooks, and knowledge resources at scale, and keep them current as programs and processes change.

Partner with the Partnership & Supply Business

  • Know the Supply Business: Build a deep understanding of how the partner and supply teams work, what partners need, what the teams are measured on, and what's changing in the lodging market.
  • Embedded Partnership: Spend regular time with partner and supply leaders, front-line managers, and reps. Join team meetings and pipeline reviews to understand needs and turn them into enablement that improves performance.
  • Rollout Support: Partner with Product, Growth, Revenue Operations, and the broader Revenue Enablement team to communicate and train on launches, process changes, and tool updates, freeing leaders to coach and sell.

Programs & Measurement

  • Measure What Matters: Track and report enablement impact for partner and supply teams, such as certification and program adoption, partner acquisition and activation, pipeline and conversion, and partner growth [TBD: confirm Partnership & Supply KPIs].
  • Performance Inspection: Drive results through inspection, evaluation, and accountability on the skills and playbooks you design.
  • Enablement Tech Stack: Make sure partner and supply teams get full value from our tools, including partner tools [TBD: confirm, e.g., PRM, Crossbeam]. Work with our tools and systems team so new tools actually get adopted.

Why This Role: AI-First at Engine
At Engine, AI isn't a side project. It's how we work. Our access to create with AI is incredibly unique, and this role is a rare chance to get exposure to a ton of AI tools and learn from the best. The expectation is simple: AI first, to create scale, so our partner and supply teams always have what they need to win. Building this way grows Engine, and it grows your skill set too. If you're growth-minded and excited to build what's next, you'll thrive here.

What You'll Bring to Engine:

We're looking for someone who's ready to make an impact and grow alongside us:

  • Experience: 4+ years in revenue enablement, sales enablement, sales training, or a customer-facing revenue role, including 2+ years designing and delivering enablement or training programs. [TBD: confirm years]
  • Partner & Supply Familiarity: Experience enabling or working on partnerships, supplier or channel teams, or account management, ideally in travel, hospitality, or a two-sided marketplace.
  • Facilitation: You can lead a room, in person or virtually, and you can turn complex programs and processes into training people actually use.
  • Business Acumen: You learn new business models quickly and can turn pipeline and performance data into a focused training or coaching response.
  • Skills: Strong project management, documentation, communication, and stakeholder management skills, and you can influence across Sales, Product, Growth, and Revenue Operations.
  • Tech-Savvy: Bonus points if you're fluent in Salesforce, conversation intelligence tools (e.g., Momentum), enablement/LMS platforms (e.g., GTMBuddy, LetterAI), and partner tools such as PRM platforms or Crossbeam.
  • AI-First Mindset: You reach for AI first to create scale, and you're excited to get hands-on with a wide range of AI tools. You're growth-minded and eager to keep building your skill set.
  • Mindset: You're ready to roll up your sleeves, work independently, and deliver results that matter.

Nice to Have:

  • Hands-on experience in hotel or lodging partnerships, supplier relations, revenue management, or OTA market management.
  • Background in B2B travel, hospitality, or marketplace businesses.
  • Experience building enablement for a new sales motion from scratch.
  • Examples of enablement content, job aids, or knowledge resources you've built with AI.

Location & Travel:This role is preferably based in or near one of our hubs in Denver, CO; Tempe, AZ; or Chicago, IL, and we're open to remote candidates elsewhere in the US. Expect to travel about one week per month to work with teams in person, plus major company events.

We accept applications for this role on an ongoing basis. We review applications as they are received and encourage interested candidates to apply early.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range
$115,600—$160,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

  • Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.
  • Benefits: Check out our full list at
  • Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

raw.description:
We are looking for an experienced pharmacovigilance medical writer to join our growing medical writing team.

What We're Looking For: A highly motivated and detail-oriented medical writer who combines strong regulatory writing expertise with a client-focused mindset and a passion for developing others. You will play a key role in delivering high-quality regulatory documents, strengthening client relationships, and supporting the growth of the wider team. The Medical Writer will be responsible for medical writing including:

Key Responsibilities:

  • Author, review, and quality check a range of regulatory and pharmacovigilance documents, including:
    • PSURs/PBRERs
    • PADERs
    • ACOs
    • DSURs
    • Risk Management Plans (RMPs)
  • Ensure documents are scientifically accurate, regulatory compliant, and delivered within agreed timelines.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyse, interpret, and present safety data effectively.
  • Act as a trusted point of contact for clients, supporting project delivery and fostering strong working relationships.
  • Provide guidance, mentoring, and knowledge sharing to junior medical writers to support their professional growth and development.
  • Contribute to process improvements and the continuous enhancement of medical writing quality standards.
  • MD, pharmacy or Life Science degree (Masters or PhD is desirable)
  • Minimum 2 years' experience in Medical Writing and associated fields (case processing, signal detection or risk management) ideally within a CRO environment
  • Ability to manage multiple and varied tasks and prioritize workload with attention to detail
  • Ability to effectively train and mentor Associate Medical Writers
  • Must be a strong team player
  • Fluency in English, an additional language is a benefit

When you join Ergomed Group, you make a difference by helping to bring safe and effective pharmaceutical treatment to patients around the world. You’ll join a passionate and collaborative team of experts in clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and quality consulting.

We are diverse in many ways, yet our values unite us. Our values are how we work, not words on a wall. If they sound like you, you will feel at home here.

  • Quality: we hold ourselves to the standard patients deserve.
  • Integrity and trust: we do the right thing, especially when it is hard.
  • Drive and passion: we care about the outcome, because someone is waiting on it.
  • Agility and responsiveness: we move quickly, because patients cannot wait.
  • Belonging: everyone is welcome, and every voice counts.
  • Collaborative partnerships: we go further by going together.

We look forward to welcoming your application.

Medicine moves forward here. So will you.

At PrimeVigilance, patient safety is not one part of the job. It is why we exist.

We are a global pharmacovigilance specialist. Our teams help clients navigate complex regulations while keeping patient safety at the center of every decision, from early development through to post-marketing surveillance. Increasingly, the value we create is not only in processing safety data but in interpreting it: spotting the signal that matters early and turning it into insight our clients can act on.

That work takes curious minds, problem-solvers and experts who care about getting it right. It also takes a culture worth staying for. Across Europe, North America, South America, Asia and Australia, we work in an environment built on kindness, flexibility, growth and belonging, where colleagues support one another and good ideas are heard wherever they come from.

If you want a role with real purpose, global reach and the chance to keep growing while you help protect patients, you will feel at home here. We would love to hear from you.

raw.title: National Sales Manager, Foodservice
raw.excerpt: OverviewDole Foods of Canada Company, part of the global Dole Packaged Foods organization, is a purpose-led company committed to championing accessible fruit nutrition and building a brighter future through the goodness of fruit.
raw.description:
Overview

Dole Foods of Canada Company, part of the global Dole Packaged Foods organization, is a purpose-led company committed to championing accessible fruit nutrition and building a brighter future through the goodness of fruit.

At Dole, our culture is uniquely driven by core Values. Our commitment to these Values transforms our work into a meaningful journey toward a brighter future together. Here, you'll be part of a respectful, inclusive culture that deeply values our colleagues, customers, and global communities. We strive for excellence, empowering each other to confidently overcome challenges, continuously learn, and achieve world-class results. Guided by unwavering integrity, our actions consistently reflect our commitment to always doing what's right, fostering lasting trust and strong relationships. Through a spirit of collaboration, we cultivate positivity, generosity, and genuine teamwork, enabling collective success toward our One Dole Purpose. Our innovative spirit leads directly to meaningful outcomes and business success.

We are looking for an ambitious, results-oriented sales leader who combines strategic thinking with relentless execution. This individual will be a true business builder, leveraging Dole’s trusted brand equity, fact based selling capabilities, and category leadership approach to accelerate growth across Canada’s foodservice channel. This leader should thrive on finding creative solutions to challenges, to achieve the long-term vision for Dole Canada.

The National Sales Manager, Foodservice will play a critical leadership role in developing and accelerating Dole Canada's Foodservice business. Reporting to the Head of Sales, Retail & Foodservice, this position is responsible for identifying new business opportunities, cultivating strategic customer relationships, and managing key national and regional accounts.

This role requires a highly commercial leader who can successfully balance business development, account management, forecasting accuracy, profitability management, and strategic planning. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to think long-term while delivering immediate results, working cross-functionally to drive profitable growth and strengthen Dole's leadership position within the Canadian marketplace.

This is based remotely in the Toronto area with flexibility to work in our Markham, Ontario office when needed.

Responsibilities

Grow and penetrate accounts in the non-commercial & commercial channels to leverage and scale Dole as a tier one supplier both regional and national basis. Implement a strategic account management focus incorporating fact-based selling, category approach, insights and culinary to key stakeholders that influence GPOs (Group Purchasing Organizations) in the local markets and nationally.

  • Develop and present a sales strategy (by promotional activities, innovation, menu planning) to achieve or exceed the objectives of the Food Service business plan.
  • Identify opportunities for new business, channels and accounts, then define strategies to penetrate and increase sales. Monitor the negotiated business plans, analyse the results, and recommend any corrective strategies.
  • Lead and plan commercial strategies and calendar for the customer and internal stakeholders to support penetration and growth.
  • Manage trade spend and optimise profitability for new and existing client/distributor agreements, tenders, and contracts. Negotiate with your client portfolio in accordance with the budget and profitability plan to ensure all business deals are profitable on both sides.
  • Develop and lead the Brokers to achieve targets and develop pipeline to ensure strategies are in line to achieve or surpass the Food Service sales objectives and business plan.
  • Develop long-term partnerships with targeted accounts that result in increased sales and margins.
  • Develop headquarter relationships with key distribution customers including GFS and Sysco.
  • Adept at relationship building beyond the buyer and the seller by establishing relationships with stakeholders who have decision making influence.
  • Understand forecasting principles to ensure excellence in contract execution to inventory management by communicating to supply chain and customer service.
  • Communicate and advise on market information and identifying emerging business opportunities.
  • Develop and manage pricing strategies long term / month to month to achieve targeted profit and volumes.
  • Work closely with the supply chain, production, and customer service teams to ensure superior customer service levels are maintained.
  • Work with the team to prepare budgets, period reviews and forecasting reports.
  • Liaise and collaborate with internal stakeholders (Marketing, Sales, Operations, Quality Control and Finance) to assist in growing the non-commercial channel.
  • Other related duties as reasonably assigned, consistent with the scope of the role

Qualifications

Experience, Knowledge, & Skills You Bring:

  • 7-10 years of progressive successful Food Service Sales experience having a renowned track record in national account management, including non-commercial foodservice account or commercial foodservice multi-unit accounts.
  • CPG account management is required.
  • Experience leading a broker network in Canada, past experience managing Affinity is a plus.
  • Exceptional time management, prioritizing and organisational skills to meet deadlines with a strong sense of urgency and a drive for results
  • Strong financial and analytical skills with a comprehension of trade, profitability, and forecasting.
  • Ability to communicate with senior leadership within Dole and externally with customers.
  • Fact based selling approach and exudes confidence in negotiations.
  • Strong project management skills
  • Proficient in MS office applications

What You’ll Need to Succeed:

  • Passionate about a purpose driven career
  • Demonstrates commitment to inclusion that support employee development and well-being
  • Establishes clear expectations and feedback loops, encourages innovation, and drives continuous improvement
  • Models and coaches towards transparency and integrity in decision-making
  • Effectively facilitates cross-team communication and teamwork

Education & Certification:

  • University degree required, preferably in Business (Bachelors or MBA)

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to sit and use the computer for extended periods of time; ability to answer phones and use a variety of office equipment; ability to lift 15 pounds and reach overhead. These physical requirements are considered essential duties of the role unless otherwise accommodated.

Travel Requirements:

  • 30-40% travel is required

This posting represents an existing vacancy.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be revised as necessary. Nothing in this job description alters the employment relationship or creates a contract of employment.

The duties may be modified to accommodate employees with disabilities.

FOR JOBS BASED IN ONTARIO:

Hiring Pay Scale: $140,000 to $160,000 CAD

Dole Packaged Foods is committed to paying our Associates fairly and equitably. The pay rate offered will consider a wide range of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, accomplishments, and location. Pay scales are subject to review on a regular basis and will be updated as appropriate.

raw.description:
Remote Account Executive, GBS LE:

Are you looking for a dynamic career with excellent advancement potential at a global market leader? If so, consider Gartner, the world's leading research and advisory company, serving C-suite leaders and their teams in 15,600+ distinct organizations in more than 100 countries. Gartner equips these leaders with the indispensable insights, advice, and tools to achieve their mission-critical priorities and build the successful organizations of tomorrow.

Account Executives are solution-oriented individuals who help clients with their most important critical challenges. The account executive is a field sales role responsible for direct client contract value retention, as well as growth through contract expansion and the introduction of new products and services. The territory for this role includes specific major client accounts and carries a sales quota of $1MM+ of contract value. Gartner is a sales-driven organization, and the success of our account executives is the fuel that grows the company. #GartnerSales

What you’ll do:

  • Consult with C-level executives to develop and implement an effective, enterprise-wide strategy that improves the value delivered by Gartner products and services

  • Manage your accounts toward an outcome of increased customer satisfaction and an increase in retention and account growth

  • Fulfill a quota responsibility of 500K+ of contract value within a territory of major client accounts

  • Handle forecast accuracy on a monthly/quarterly/annual basis

What you need:

  • 6 – 10 years of external experience with validated consultative sales, with evidence of prior success

  • Proficiency in account planning and an understanding of territory management

  • The ability to prospect and run C-level and senior-level relationships within midsize and large organizations

  • Demonstrated intellect, drive, executive presence and sales acumen

  • Proven experience building excellent client relationships through offering beneficial, insightful and strategic insights into their businesses

  • Strong proficiency in computer skills

  • Excellent written and oral presentation skills

  • Knowledge of the full life cycle of the sales process, from prospecting to close

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 102,000 USD - 147,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Our talent acquisition team will provide the specific opportunity on our bonus or incentive programs to eligible candidates. We also offer market leading benefit programs including generous PTO, a 401k match up to $7,200 per year, the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount, and more.

description: What We Can Achieve Together: The Division Finance Director, Great Plains oversees the strategy, analysis, and management of financial activities and contracts services for the Great Plains Division, which covers 10 states: Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, and Texas.

raw.title: Division Finance Director, Great Plains
raw.excerpt: What We Can Achieve Together: The Division Finance Director, Great Plains oversees the strategy, analysis, and management of financial activities and contracts services for the Great Plains Division, which covers 10 states: Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, and Texas.
raw.description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


The Division Finance Director, Great Plains oversees the strategy, analysis, and management of financial activities and contracts services for the Great Plains Division, which covers 10 states: Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, and Texas. They serve as a thought partner to the Great Plains Division Director and Division Leadership Team in decision making, budgeting, and resource allocation. The position works across the Great Plains Division to strengthen financial strategy, stewardship, alignment, and decision support. They also collaborate with Division leadership and Legal to ensure that the Contracts team is providing timely, effective support to Great Plains Business Units.


The DFD provides broad oversight of Great Plains Division finances, including planning, reporting, and analysis of current finance and operations activities. They identify gaps in alignment and opportunities for efficiency and ensure financial management standards and compliance requirements are met. The DFD represents the Great Plains Division in regional and organization-wide initiatives and tailors implementation for the Division. This includes effectively addressing challenging situations that could affect the Division’s long-term financial or operational position. As needed, the DFD works across the organization to resolve high-priority issues, such as process gaps that impact business processes.


The DFD is responsible for synthesizing financial information for senior leaders and developing creative financial strategies that direct resources toward critical work. They drive improved financial performance and reduce financial and operational risk by identifying trends, anticipating challenges, and translating insights into actions that strengthen the Division’s financial position.They provide subject matter expertise, serve as a resource to the Great Plains Management Team, and drive alignment across the Division. The DFD manages the newly formed Great Plains Division Finance team, an organization of 18 staff members that includes six direct reports, and is accountable for setting direction, building team capability, and ensuring coordinated delivery of finance and contracts support services across the Division. This position reports to the North America Region Finance Director with a dotted line to the Great Plains Division Director.


RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE

  • Develops and implements financial strategy for the Great Plains Division, including resource deployment, risk management, and financial health.
  • Leads and manages the newly formed Great Plains Division Finance team of 18 staff members, including six direct reports; establishes team priorities, develops staff capabilities, manages performance, and ensures coordinated, high-quality finance and contracts support across the Division.
  • Delivers financial expertise, thought partnership, and decision-making support to the Great Plains Division Director, Great Plains Division Leadership Team, and Business Unit Finance staff.
  • Provides divisional leadership and influence by shaping cross-functional priorities, strengthening alignment among Pods and business units, and advancing finance-informed decisions across the Great Plains Division.
  • Leads long-range financial planning and sustainability efforts, including scenario analysis and strategic resource allocation to balance near-term priorities with long-term conservation and organizational needs.
  • Translates complex financial information into clear, decision-oriented insights and recommendations for executive leaders.
  • Partners with philanthropy and fundraising leaders to align financial strategy with revenue goals, assess funding opportunities, and develop sustainable funding approaches for divisional priorities.
  • Collaborates with Great Plains stakeholders on organization-wide initiatives, including Workday stabilization, and the operations and funding model, and tailors implementation for the Great Plains Division.
  • Leads planning, reporting, and analysis for Great Plains Division finances, including development of the Division budget.
  • Provides broad oversight of Great Plains Division Finance and Contracts activities to ensure financial management standards and compliance requirements are met.
  • Responsible for overseeing the Contracts Manager, who leads a team supporting contracts, procurement, purchasing, agreement workflows, documentation, and compliance across the Great Plains Division.
  • Manages and directs the implementation of multiple projects in a strategic, integrated and collaborative approach.
  • Decisions may have program-wide impact and may bind the organization or organizational unit financially and legally.
  • Ensures programmatic commitments, TNC policies and procedures, financial standards and legal requirements are met and managed for ethical compliance.
  • Reports to senior leadership on functional activities.

We’re Looking for You:


Are you looking for work you can believe in? At TNC we strive to embody a philosophy of Work that You Can Believe in where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong experience in leading a diverse, multi-disciplinary team. The ideal candidate should have exceptional communication and collaboration skills and experience designing, organizing, and directing complex projects. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of our team!


What You’ll Bring:

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or related field and 7 years related work experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience with accounting principles, practices, and regulations.
  • Experience implementing or managing financial systems.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with financial management of an enterprise or sizable organizational unit.
  • Ability to resolve complex issues collaboratively and proactively.
  • Professional certification as a CPA or CIA.
  • Ability to foster an environment of creativity and professional growth.
  • Extensive management experience including ability to motivate, lead, set objectives, and manage performance of a large multi-disciplinary team.
  • Advanced knowledge of current and evolving trends in relevant discipline.
  • Successful experience in developing, directing and managing multiple projects.
  • Superb communication and presentation skills.
  • Experience acting as a resource to others to solve problems.

Salary Information:

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $136,850-$185,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

As we grow, integrations are becoming an increasingly important part of how customers build with Tailscale. We're looking for an Integration Partnerships Lead to help identify, develop, and launch the technical partnerships that extend our products and make Tailscale more valuable alongside the tools our customers already use.

This is a hands-on technical partnerships role at the intersection of Sales Engineering and Partner Development. You'll work directly with technology partners, customers, Product, and Engineering to identify integration opportunities, understand technical requirements, design solutions, establish the partnership, and help take integrations from concept through launch and adoption.

You'll initially focus on integrations across Aperture, Privileged Access Management (PAM), and VPN, working with partners across AI, security, identity, infrastructure, developer tools, and adjacent technologies.

We're looking for someone who can move comfortably between a technical architecture conversation and a commercial partnership discussion. You should be able to understand how two products work together, explain the customer value, navigate APIs and integration requirements, build relationships with technical and business stakeholders, and drive both organizations toward a successful launch.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identify and develop high-value technology and integration partnerships based on customer needs, product priorities, and market opportunities.
  • Own partner opportunities from initial outreach and technical discovery through solution design, commercial alignment, launch, and ongoing adoption.
  • Lead technical discovery with partners and customers to understand architectures, APIs, authentication, security requirements, data flows, and integration use cases.
  • Work closely with Product and Engineering to assess technical feasibility, define integration requirements, and determine the right implementation approach.
  • Build trusted relationships across partner Product, Engineering, Sales, and Business Development teams while serving as the primary point of contact at Tailscale.
  • Develop the technical and business case for integrations, including customer value, use cases, implementation requirements, and commercial opportunity.
  • Partner with Legal and Finance on agreements, pricing, packaging, licensing, and revenue-sharing structures where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Marketing, and Customer Success to launch integrations and drive customer and partner adoption.
  • Bring customer, partner, and market feedback back to Product and Engineering to help inform future integration priorities.
  • Help establish repeatable approaches for evaluating, building, launching, and scaling technology partnerships as the ecosystem grows.

What We Are Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience across Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Technical Partnerships, Partner Engineering, Technology Alliances, Partner Sales, or technical Business Development in B2B software.
  • Strong technical fluency across APIs, authentication, cloud infrastructure, networking, security, developer platforms, or modern SaaS integrations.
  • Experience leading technical discovery and translating customer or partner requirements into practical integration solutions.
  • Demonstrated ability to explain complex technical concepts to both engineering teams and business stakeholders.
  • Experience developing technology partnerships from initial opportunity through technical validation, commercial agreement, and launch.
  • Strong commercial instincts with experience identifying customer value, building business cases, negotiating, and navigating complex partner organizations.
  • Ability to influence Product and Engineering teams without formal authority while maintaining credibility with technical stakeholders.
  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-moving environment where the solution, partnership model, or playbook may not yet exist.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with developer infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, identity, cloud infrastructure, AI/LLM platforms, or developer tools.
  • Experience working with APIs, SDKs, OAuth/OIDC, SSO, identity providers, webhooks, connectors, or other common integration patterns.
  • Experience in a product-led or developer-first company.
  • Experience with ISV, technology alliance, marketplace, OEM, or cloud partner ecosystems.
  • Experience working with both emerging technology companies and large enterprise partners.

Reporting Structure

This role reports to Kevin Kotecki, President and CRO, and will work closely with Avery Pennarun (Co-Founder & CEO), David Carney (Co-Founder & CSO), Product, Engineering, Sales, and Solutions Engineering to develop and launch Tailscale's most important technology integrations.

As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.

CAN Pay Range
$402,000—$402,000 CAD

What We Offer

  • An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.
  • A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).
  • Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family!
  • Remote first company—most of our teams work fully remotely. Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). Some roles require in-office collaboration depending on team needs, which will be clearly noted in the job description.
  • Employer-funded retirement contributions. Tailscale will match your retirement contributions dollar-for-dollar, up to a maximum annual employer contribution equal to 0.75% of your eligible compensation.
  • Connect with other Tailscalars IRL. Attend our annual company retreat, participate in team off-sites, and collaborate in person with teammates across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. We support intentional in-person connection through team travel and distributed collaboration.
  • Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities.
  • Paid time off and a healthy work-life integration. Our flexible, paid time off program supports you for any situation life throws your way, whether moving homes or travelling the world!
  • A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own.
  • Paid parental leave program. We care about your life outside of work and encourage new parents to take advantage of parental leave top-ups (20 weeks for birthing parents, 16 weeks for non-birthing parents).
